_spec: Stage 0 expected output. Written from the migration journal SPEC (web/drizzle/migrations/meta/_journal.json + its .sql files) BEFORE the rebuild was ever run, per the T-403-round-2 lesson against after-the-fact acceptance tests. Regenerating this file from a live database is a defect, not a fix: if the DB disagrees, the DB (or the journal) is wrong.
_note: Issue #251: the journal does NOT fully rebuild schema.ts state (ipos 32/55 cols, documents 8/19). A journal-rebuilt DB is valid for migration-path tests, not for full-schema fixtures. Therefore this expectation covers TABLE PRESENCE and EMPTINESS only, never column sets.
_journalEntriesNote: journalEntries MUST be bumped by any slice that adds a JOURNALED migration - it is a hard count, not derived, and it counts meta/_journal.json entries only. s1 of the pull-model implementation loop bumped 35->36 (20260909153933_sloppy_morph.sql: 3 ADD COLUMN + 3 CREATE INDEX, no new table/enum). s2 (unique constraints on promoters/peer_companies/ipo_intermediaries) does NOT bump this: its DDL (web/drizzle/migrations/_gated/E1_row_key_unique_constraints.sql) is deliberately kept OUT of meta/_journal.json per the migration rule (adding gated DDL to the journal is what drops production columns/breaks unbackfilled slots) - verified by grep against _journal.json before this note was written. A later slice's JOURNALED migration must still bump this; a slice whose DDL stays gated must not. s3 (row_key widening on field_sources/data_conflicts) BUMPS this 36->37: 20260910043758_salty_shen.sql adds the row_key column (ADD COLUMN, additive) to both tables plus two CREATE INDEX / one DROP INDEX statements, and IS in meta/_journal.json (verified by grep before this note was written). The field_sources unique-constraint widen+rename that was originally planned for s3 (renaming unique_field_source_per_ipo to a row-scoped name) was dropped from scope in a re-scope on 2026-09-10: schema.ts still declares the original 3-column unique_field_source_per_ipo constraint (ipo_id, table_name, field_name), unchanged from main, and no migration (journaled or gated) touches it. There is no F1 gated constraint file for this slice. A row-key-scoped constraint is deferred to a later slice. s6 (risk-factor row key: (ipo_id, seq) -> (ipo_id, heading_hash)) BUMPS this 37->38: 20260910121813_cooing_manta.sql adds the heading_hash column (ADD COLUMN heading_hash varchar(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT '', additive) and IS in meta/_journal.json (verified by grep before this note was written). s6's constraint swap - DROP unique_ipo_risk_factors_ipo_seq, ADD unique_ipo_risk_factors_ipo_heading_hash - lives in web/drizzle/migrations/_gated/E2_risk_factor_heading_hash_key.sql and deliberately does NOT bump this, same rule as s2's E1 (verified by grep against meta/_journal.json before this note was written: the gated file's tag/name does not appear there). Item 18 slice 1 BUMPS this 38->39: 20260910180241_military_logan.sql creates the document_pages table, adds documents.purged_unread (ADD COLUMN, additive, NOT NULL with a default so it is safe on existing rows), adds the FK and one CREATE INDEX, and IS in meta/_journal.json at idx 38 (verified by reading the journal after generation). The migration was REGENERATED on the repaired snapshot chain rather than carried over: the branch was first cut when the journal ended at 37, and its original migration (20260910145911_left_speed) had been generated against a snapshot that predated two merged migrations - carrying that over is precisely what broke db:generate repo-wide (#533). The regenerated snapshot's prevId chains to the current head exactly, and row_key and heading_hash are both still present in it. It also adds "document_pages" to the expected table set above - a new TABLE must be added there as well as bumping the count, which the count alone does not cover. Item 22 slice 4 BUMPS this 39->40: 20260910183358_small_freak.sql adds documents.part_number (integer, NULLABLE, no default) and documents.exchange_document_id (varchar(255), NULLABLE, no default), and IS in meta/_journal.json at idx 39. It adds NO table, so the expected table set above is unchanged - a count bump without a table addition is correct here, and the two are deliberately separate assertions. Both columns are nullable ON PURPOSE: a NOT NULL default of 1 for part_number would make all 258 existing document rows claim to be part one of a multi-part filing, a value nobody measured reading as though somebody had. Item 1 slice s18 BUMPS this 40->41: 20260910191610_handy_night_nurse.sql swaps field_sources' unique_field_source_per_ipo from (ipo_id, table_name, field_name) to (ipo_id, table_name, row_key, field_name) - the widening s3 deferred, so the s3 sentence above is now history, not current state. It is JOURNALED, not gated: adding a column to a unique key strictly weakens it, so no existing row can violate the new form (verified read-only: zero duplicate groups under the widened key on ipodhan_staging over 8,092 rows and on ipodhan_test), which means there is nothing to repair first and no order dependency the journal cannot express. The constraint NAME is deliberately unchanged - see the build card's "Reversal" section. Item 4 (per-field validation, OD-21) BUMPS this 41->42: 20260910224504_numerous_unus.sql creates the field_extraction_failures table (one row per field a validation rule rejected before the write), its two FKs (ipo_id CASCADE, document_id SET NULL) and four indexes, and IS in meta/_journal.json at idx 41 (verified by reading the journal after generation; the generated .sql was read end to end and contains that table and nothing else). It DOES add a table, so field_extraction_failures is added to the expected table set above as well - alphabetically, between extraction_logs and field_protection_metadata, because that list is sorted and a list that is sorted except for its newest entry stops being readable in a diff. The count was confirmed by counting pgTable declarations in packages/shared/src/db/schema.ts (37) and diffing them against this list, not by trusting the failing assertion's arithmetic: the CI message read as 35->36, the real move is 36->37. Item 5 slice 1 (the ipo_field_plan table + generator) BUMPS this 42->43: 20260911002839_nostalgic_mantis.sql creates the ipo_field_plan table (one row per (IPO, table, field) recording what the pull walk ASKED and what came back, because field_sources records only successful writes so a field never attempted and a field attempted-and-failed are both simply absent), its two FKs (ipo_id CASCADE, chosen_document_id SET NULL) and four indexes, and IS in meta/_journal.json at idx 42. It DOES add a table, so ipo_field_plan is added to the expected table set above as well, alphabetically between ipo_details and ipo_financials. IMPORTANT: the migration also creates the ENUM TYPE field_plan_state - an enum is NOT a table and is deliberately NOT added to this list; adding it would assert a table that will never exist. The count was verified by counting pgTable declarations in packages/shared/src/db/schema.ts (38) and diffing against this list (37, difference exactly one), not by trusting the failing assertion arithmetic - per the warning earlier in this note. Item 5 slice 2 (#618) BUMPS this 43->44: 20260911033922_nice_baron_zemo.sql widens ipo_field_plan's unique_ipo_field_plan from (ipo_id, table_name, field_name) to (ipo_id, table_name, row_key, field_name) -- financial_statements holds one row per fiscal year, so two years' plan rows for the same field collided under the old key. It ADD COLUMNs row_key varchar(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT '' (additive, safe on the table's zero existing rows -- verified against meta/_journal.json, this table's own creating migration is idx 42, one before this one at idx 43), DROPs the old constraint and ADDs the widened one, and IS in meta/_journal.json at idx 43 (verified by reading the journal after generation). It adds NO table, so the expected table set above is unchanged.
